:::{#def-binomial}
#### Binomial distribution

A [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) random variable $X$
has the **binomial distribution**
with number of trials $n \in \set{1, 2, \dots}$
and event probability $\prob \in [0, 1]$,
written $X \sim \dBinf{n, \prob}$
[@wikipedia_binomial_distribution],
if:

$$
\P(X = x) \eqdef \binom{n}{x} \prob^x (1 - \prob)^{n - x},
\quad x \in \set{0, 1, \dots, n}
$$ {#eq-binom-pmf}

where $\binom{n}{x} = \frac{n!}{x!\,(n - x)!}$
is the number of ways to choose $x$ of the $n$ trials.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

@CaseBerg01 [Section 3.2] defines the binomial distribution the same way.
With $n = 1$, @eq-binom-pmf is the
[Bernoulli PMF](random-variables.qmd#def-bernoulli):
$\dBinf{1, \prob}$ and $\Ber(\prob)$ are the same distribution.

:::
